thread.title: Big, Bold Blue-Chip Buys: GE, Pfizer, Disney, Apple - Barron's

title: Big, Bold Blue-Chip Buys: GE, Pfizer, Disney, Apple - Barron's
text:
Ed Lin Feb. 2, 2018 1:54 p.m. ET
Last April, Gary Ran, chairman and chief executive of Telemus Capital, told our colleagues at The Wall Street Journal that his clients who voted against Donald Trump in the presidential election weren’t opposed to the market rally that followed .
“[T]hey’re enjoying the benefits. No one is telling me, ‘I’m afraid of Trump,’ at this point, as far as their investments go,” said Ran. We appreciate that Telemus is based in Southfield, Mich., a city where Hillary Clinton received nearly nine times the number of votes than Trump in the 2016 election .
If anyone can help his clients make the best of any situation, Ran has the skill set. He came in fourth place in Barron’s 2017 ranking of top advisors for Michigan. Telemus manages more than $2 billion in assets and the average account stands at $3.5 million.
What moves did Telemus make in the fourth quarter? A recent disclosure shows the advisor bulked up on four components of the Dow Jones Industrial Average: General Electric (ticker: GE); Disney (DIS); Pfizer (PFE); and Apple (AAPL). It also made a massive purchase of shares of Illinois Tool Works (ITW).
After GE shares lost half their value in 2017 , investors wondered if the elevator had stopped at the ground floor. It turned out that there were a number of sub-basements, as well. Through midday trading Friday, GE is down wider than 10% for the year-to-date, pummeled by potential regulatory issues and speculation it could be removed as a component of the Dow Jones Industrial Average . Telemus bought nearly 83,000 more GE shares in the fourth quarter, more than tripling its ownership to 115,600 shares at the end of 2017.
Disney shares played a game of cat-and-mouse with upside in 2017, eking out a gain of nearly 5%, excluding dividends, in the end. Telemus bet there was more in store for the stock, and bought nearly 29,000 more Disney shares, more than quadrupling its investment to 38,500 shares. Come January, however, investors were concerned that Disney’s latest Star Wars film didn’t storm the box office as expected . Nonetheless, the stock is up 2% so far this year.
After a respectable 16% gain in 2017, Pfizer shares have tacked on an additional 3% in 2018. We suggested the pharmaceutical giant could see a windfall from the sale of its consumer brands including ChapStick and Advil. Telemus was bullish on Pfizer in the last quarter of 2017 and more than tripled holdings to 66,100 shares by buying 47,200 additional shares.
Telemus bought 57,300 more shares of Apple in the fourth quarter, bringing its investment to 141,000 shares. The iPhone maker’s shares were already up for the year in that quarter and ended 2017 with a 48% gain. Apple continues to post record results, even if phone sales disappoint and its outlook calls for less upside . Shares are down 4% so far in 2018.
Unlike Apple, Illinois Tool Works is a company that doesn’t grab headlines, but we appreciate the company for what it is : a multi-industrial manufacturer with a stock for value pickers. The company doubled the 20% gain posted by the Standard & Poor’s 500 Index in 2017 with little fanfare. It continues to appreciate to little public appreciation; shares are up 3% so far in 2018. Telemus backed up the trailer truck to buy the stock, purchasing 295,000 shares in the fourth quarter, bringing total holdings to 297,000 shares.
The Illinois Tool Works purchase isn’t a surprise, as Telemus’s Ran told the Journal he was looking at opportunities that would thrive under Trump, including infrastructure, which is one of the company’s sweet spots. Judging by the moves that Telemus has recently made, it has found something to console clients who are would-be blue-state voters: blue chips.
